title: Operational Onboarding Accelerator for Service Safety and SLOs
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a working guide to accelerate cross-team handoffs for service safety (SLO-driven) across product, platform, and operations. The doc focuses on concrete gates, minimum instrumentation, and a lightweight rollout sequence that teams can follow in a 6–12 week window.

Why this exists:
- We repeatedly see feature teams ship partial telemetry or ambiguous error definitions, which slows SLO adoption and creates rework for SREs.
- Goal: reduce average time-to-first-SLO from 10+ weeks to 4–6 weeks by standardizing the minimum checklist and the handoff ritual.

Audience:
- Product and feature engineers preparing a service for SLO adoption
- Platform/SRE engineers accepting new SLOs into the monitoring and alerting fabric
- Program managers coordinating rollout windows and stakeholder comms

Key principles (stated simply):
1) Minimum viable observability: ship the smallest set of signals that permit a reliable judgement about availability and latency for the customer experience slice.
2) Gate-first approach: meet a small set of objective gates before SREs will onboard an SLO.
3) Fast feedback loop: instrument, evaluate for 2 weeks in prod mirror or dark traffic, then iterate.
4) Human-centered alerts: reduce noisy alerts by leaning on error budgets, not single-instance alarms.

Handoff timeline (recommended 6–8 weeks):
- Week 0: Intake & alignment workshop (1h) — product, engineers, SRE liaison, PM. Outcome: primary customer journey, critical API endpoints, expected traffic patterns, and an owner.
- Week 1: Instrumentation sprint (2 days focused) — add request-level outcome tags, latency histograms, and high-cardinality identifiers for sampling.
- Week 2: Metric smoke tests + synthetic checks — verify metrics appear, sampling is sane, histograms show expected buckets.
- Weeks 3–4: Observability rehearsal — use canary or dark traffic to exercise SLO queries and alerting rules. Iterate on thresholds.
- Week 5: SRE acceptance review — SRE confirms gates met and schedules onboarding into team dashboards and oncall playbooks.
- Week 6+: Release & monitor — error budget tracking enabled; weekly health reviews for first 30 days.

Minimum instrumentation (MVI) checklist — team must complete these for an SRE handoff:
- Request outcome metric: a counter with labelled outcomes (success / client_error / server_error / throttled) by route or customer segment.
- Latency histogram: p50/p90/p99 and exponential histogram or defined buckets for request latency.
- Request sampling: trace id or request id added to logs for a 0.1% sampled trace; distributed tracing enabled for critical flows.
- Dependency signals: downstream call error rates and latencies (at least coarse counters).
- Synthetic health check: a lightweight end-to-end probe that exercises the happy path and a degraded path.
- Deployability metadata: service name, version, cluster/region, and a minimal runbook link in deployment metadata.

Acceptance gates (must be met for SRE to own SLO tracking):
- Metrics present in monitoring for 7 days with sane cardinality (no label explosion).
- Alert rule prototype exists that uses error budget burn as primary trigger, not raw 5xx spikes.
- Tracing sample spans for three distinct customer journeys verified.
- Synthetic probe results show <1% flakiness over 48 hours.
- Runbook stub added to repo with how to escalate and rollback.

Recommended SLO taxonomy (suggested defaults):
- Availability SLO: % of successful requests (success / (success + server_error + throttled)) over a rolling 30d window. Target depends on tier (e.g., 99.5% for critical APIs, 99.0% for non-critical).
- Latency SLO: % of requests below acceptable p90 threshold, measured on production traffic (rolling 30d).
- Freshness/validity SLO (for async flows): lag-based objective on queue processing time.

Alerting & response pattern (practical formula):
- Primary alert: error-budget burn-rate sustained > 3x expected for 30m -> paging to oncall.
- Secondary alert: degradation window (e.g., rising p99) -> routed to engineering channel, not immediate pager.
- Tactical: create a triage checklist that includes 'is this caused by a dependency?', 'recent deploys?', 'config/traffic change?'.

Communication templates (short):
- Intake message (to SRE liaison): "Intake: service X, owner @<engineer>, primary endpoint /v1/foo, expected peak qps: 200, initial SLO target: 99.5 availability. Instrumentation PR: <link>. Can we schedule acceptance review week of YYYY-MM-DD?"
- Onboarding confirmation: "SRE acceptance complete. SLO enabled in dashboards, synthetic checks added, runbook: <link>. Oncall pager: <policy>. First 30d weekly health: Mondays 10:30am PT."

Common pitfalls we want to avoid:
- Over-labeling metrics: leads to high cardinality and monitoring bills. Provide recommended label set (route, region, status_class, customer_tier).
- Measuring client-side errors as server failures — ensure client vs server error semantics are clear.
- Wiring alerts to raw counts rather than normalized burn rates.

Roles & responsibilities (one-liners):
- Feature engineering team: implement MVI, author runbook stub, fix instrumentation gaps.
- SRE liaison: review metrics, verify gates, own error budget integration and dashboard creation.
- Product/PM: define primary customer journeys and acceptance criteria for SLO targets.
- Security/Platform: validate any new tracing/backpressure that impacts PII or throughput.

Template snippets (copy-paste friendly) — example PromQL fragments: (note: adapt to our metrics naming)
- Availability: sum(rate(service_requests_total{job=~"svc-.*",status!~"4.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(service_requests_total{job=~"svc-.*"}[5m]))
- Latency p90: histogram_quantile(0.90, sum(rate(service_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- Error budget burn: (1 - availability_window) / (window_length) scaled to burn rate (team-specific)

Operational checklist for first 30 days after onboarding:
- Day 0: enable dashboards, confirm synthetic probes, create incident template for the service.
- Day 3: check alert noise; suppress or refine any noisy rules.
- Day 7: validate traces for at least two non-trivial incidents (postmortem practise).
- Day 14: calibrate thresholds based on observed traffic shape.
- Day 30: product + SRE retrospective; decide on tiering and long-term SLO targets.

Open questions / decisions to make (for the initial workshop):
- Do we accept client-side timeouts as failures for availability SLOs? (proposal: only if they map to a server response code or inferred server-side resource constraints)
- Default SLO target per service tier (we need product input).
- Sampling rate for traces vs cost tradeoff (ops to propose defaults).

Next actions (owner tags and short deadlines):
- @Asha: draft instrumentation PR template with labels and example metric names by 2026-02-18.
- @Tom: prepare an onboarding checklist in monitoring repo and link to dashboards by 2026-02-23.
- @Claire (owner): schedule intake workshop and produce a canonical intake form by 2026-02-16.

Notes to self / heuristics:
- If a team cannot meet MVI in 2 weeks, escalate to program manager to re-evaluate scope.
- Favor a pragmatic SLO (measure what matters) over theoretical perfect coverage.
- Keep the initial SLO narrow (one customer journey) and expand after 30 days.

Revision history (short):
- 2026-02-12: initial draft + intake template.
- 2026-02-20: added PromQL snippets and first-run checklist.
- 2026-03-03: clarified acceptance gates and added owners for next actions.

End of doc.
